quote: Now is the winter of our discontent made glorious summer by this sun of York.
source: William Shakespeare, Richard III, Act 1, scene 1, lines 1 to 2 (Richard, Duke of Gloucester)
speaker: Richard, Duke of Gloucester

evidence.where: The Globe text (Clark and Wright) as served by the MIT Shakespeare site, which prints sun of York; the Folger edition was also checked and prints son of York
evidence.edition: The Globe Shakespeare (Clark and Wright, 1864), the reading also of the Arden, Riverside and Penguin editions
evidence.locator: Richard III, 1.1.1 to 2, the opening soliloquy

reason: The two opening lines are exact in the Globe, Arden, Riverside and Penguin texts; the early quartos and the Folio print Son of Yorke and the Folger keeps son, so sun is the majority modernised reading, not a mint. The semicolon that ends line 2 becomes the full stop the card needs. The speaker is the villain and the source names him, as the Polonius rule requires.
